Independently reconstructed Jensen function convexity from its positive-coefficient power series and equality support; the 318 stored package cases were inspected as code, not re-run as a separate scientific certificate.
correctness.rationale: For Poisson orientation increments, uniform Haar law is stationary and jump-reversal sends P to reflected P^R; the jump-relative-entropy rate is exactly α KL(P||P^R), not total physical heat. With ν=(P+P^R)/2 and odd u=(dP−dP^R)/(dP+dP^R), one obtains c=∫cosψ dν, s=∫sinψ u dν and KL=∫g(u²)dν, g(t)=2sqrt(t)atanh sqrt(t)=2Σ_{j≥1}t^j/(2j−1). Cauchy–Schwarz and Jensen yield ∫u²≥s²/(1−c²), KL≥2r atanhr. Equality for nonzero s forces cosψ=c almost surely and unique mirrored two-atom law at ±arccos c with weights (1±s/sqrt(1−c²))/2. Reflection-symmetric laws attain zero for s=0. Disjoint smooth symmetric bumps preserve both first moments with KL→minimum. Unit-circle boundary is either a reflection-fixed deterministic turn (zero cost) or a nonfixed deterministic turn (infinite cost). The required c²+s²<1 and α>0 boundaries are explicit.

value.rationale: The first Fourier turn moment determines observable persistence rate and angular drift but not underlying jump irreversibility. The sharp variational solution gives the precise least stationary orientation-path entropy rate compatible with these observables, including a unique atomic strategy for nonzero chirality, smooth-density approximation, and exact extreme boundaries. It is motivated by an intrinsic inference/design question, not arbitrary numerical optimization; physical heat/other degrees of freedom are explicitly excluded.
